terms.comment: Any made likeness of a thing: a statue, an image, a working model. A toy version of something is described with lūsōrius.
Traupman’s word; classically a copy or a pattern rather than a miniature.

evidence: Cic. N. D. 1.103: effigiēs hominis et imāgō (Lewis & Short)

phrases.latin: simulācrum columbae ē lignō ab Archȳtā ratiōne quādam disciplīnāque mēchanicā factum volāsse
phrases.english: (they say) that a wooden model of a dove, made by Archytas with some method and mechanical skill, flew

sources: Lewis & Short: simulacrum · Lewis & Short: exemplar · Lewis & Short: effigies
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, p. 346, checked against the searchable text of the book (9 November 2026).
Quotations from the Latinitas loci collections (loci-gellius), checked against the editions named there.
